svg.title: Who may do what, and where?
svg.desc: Three questions in order. 1, who is calling: verify the configured issuer, audience, client and token type, and resolve provider, issuer and subject to a linked local principal. 2, may this person or service do this here: check local grants for tenant, project, environment and resource; application services enforce the same checks as HTTP requests. 3, which data may the transaction touch: set transaction-local tenant context in the unit of work, and PostgreSQL row-level security and scoped composite keys bound the data. Secrets need their own admission check: scoped secret handles resolve only for authorized work and approved destinations, and migration owner, application, scheduler and worker identities stay separate. Provider role claims, URL IDs and compiler success never grant permission.
svg.text: Who may do what, and where?
A valid identity is the start of authorization, not its conclusion.
Verify the configured issuer, audience, client and token type.
Resolve the provider / issuer / subject to a local principal.
May this person or service do this here?
Check local grants for tenant, project, environment and resource.
Application services enforce the same checks as HTTP requests.
Which data may the transaction touch?
Set transaction-local tenant context in the unit of work.
PostgreSQL RLS and scoped composite keys bound the data.
Secrets need their own admission check.
Resolve scoped secret handles only for authorized work and approved destinations.
Migration owner, application, scheduler and worker identities remain separate.
Provider role claims, URL IDs and compiler success do not grant permission.

g.text: Identity says who called; current scoped grants decide what they may do.
